newsitem.title: USA: Dow climbs to its third record close in a row.
newsitem.headline: Dow climbs to its third record close in a row.

text.p: The Dow Jones industrial average set its third straight record close Thursday after a fast-paced recovery from a bout of profit taking.
The Dow ended up 28.57 points at a new high of 8,116.93, which surpassed Wednesday's milestone of 8,088.38. Early in the day, the index plunged more than 90 points.
But in the broader market, declining issues led advances 1,450 to 1,367 on active volume of 571 million shares on the New York Stock Exchange.
The Standard & Poor's and the New York Stock Exchange composite indexes also climbed to new highs.
The session saw stocks succumb to profit-taking, only to rebound sharply in late trading as investors proved themselves willing to buy even on the slightest of dips.
The bull market offered a show of resilience, with the Dow bouncing back sharply from a brief foray below 8,000 on continued strong volume.
"As the market goes to higher and higher levels, you have to show there's real demand for stocks to continue," said Greg Nie, technical analyst at Everen Securities.
"We've been able to do that with record volume last week and more decent volume," he said.
International Business Machines Corp. was strongest among Dow components, gaining 2-3/4 to 107-7/8.
SoundView Financial raised its one-year target price on IBM to $124 from $100, saying that recent gains nothwithstanding, the giant computer maker remained a relatively inexpensive stock.
While analysts believe that the market would eventually pause in its record-shattering run, few though the current leg of the bull market was apt to reverse itself soon.

"This has been a very powerful advance the likes of which is very infrequently seen," said Joseph Barthel, chief investment strategist at Fahnestock & Co. "There are many things coming into focus that make this market different."

Those factors include strong mutual fund inflows and corporate earnings growth, and an apparent green light from Federal Reserve Chairman Alan Greenspan, whose Humphrey-Hawkins testimony to Congress this week dispelled fears of an imminent interest rate increase.
Also helping is a resurgent dollar, which soared to a six-year high against the German mark and a 3-1/2-year peak against the Swiss franc in Thursday's trading.

While analysts have cautioned that long-term strength of the dollar can hurt profit growth at U.S. multinationals, that effect is more than offset in the short-run by the increased investment money it attracts to stocks from abroad.
Among individual issues, Digital Equipment Corp. rose 2-7/8 to 42-5/8 after reporting quarterly profits that beat Wall Street estimates.
Nellcor Puritan Bennett Inc. surged 7-1/8 to 28-1/16 after agreeing to a $1.9 billion takeover bid from fellow medical product supplier Mallinckrodt Inc., whose stock fell 1-1/2 to 38-1/4.
Microsoft Corp. lost 3-7/16 to 138 after the company said it expected its research and marketing expenses would rise in 1998.
The Nasdaq Composite index gained 1.48 points to 1,569.13.
The Standard & Poor's composite index of 500 stocks rose 3.72 to 940.28, a record. The American Stock Exchange index rose 2.40 to 637.05.
The NYSE Composite index of all listed common stocks rose 1.80 to 487.31, a record. The average share was up 17 cents.
The Wilshire Associates Equity Index -- the market value of NYSE, American and Nasdaq issues -- was at a new high 8,894.449, up 30.385, or 0.35 percent.
